backlog.spec: Build a three-member rank-averaged ensemble out of the three model families that have each scored at or below the incumbent on their own. Member 1: ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=800, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on the current descriptor+pharmacophore matrix. Member 2: CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the same matrix. Member 3: the existing 5-seed MLPClassifier ensemble on the quantile-normal transform. Rank-normalize each member's probabilities and average with equal weights 1/3. Drop the RandomForest entirely. Keep total runtime under 10 minutes; if CatBoost is slow, reduce it to 400 iterations.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees + CatBoost + MLP equal rank blend

backlog.spec: Add a LightGBM ranker (objective='lambdarank' or 'rank_xendcg', one query group containing all training rows, 300 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, colsample 0.3) trained on the same descriptor plus pharmacophore matrix. Its raw scores approximate pairwise AUROC-style ordering, which matches the metric. Rank-normalise its test scores and average them with the RF and MLP ranks with equal weights 1/3 each. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking LightGBM as blend member

backlog.spec: Replace the hard-coded 0.5/0.5 rank average with a weight picked from the training fold. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 4-fold GroupKFold over the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES string when it fails), to collect out-of-fold RF and MLP scores (use 2 MLP seeds inside the inner loop to stay fast). Pick w from the grid 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 that maximizes inner AUROC of w * rank(RF) + (1 - w) * rank(MLP), then refit both models on the full training fold (5 MLP seeds as now) and return the blend with that w. Keep features and models unchanged and make sure the inner loop keeps 15 fits under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Blend weight chosen by inner scaffold-grouped CV

backlog.spec: Replace the MLPClassifier with MLPRegressor trained on soft targets (y*0.9+0.05), using the same hidden sizes (256,64), alpha 1e-2 and early_stopping. Use 5 seeds and average the outputs. Rank-blend with the RF as before.
backlog.title: Label-smoothed MLP via regression

backlog.spec: Train 8 MLPs, each on a random 60% subset of the quantile-normal feature columns. Draw the subset with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Average their probabilities, then rank-blend with the RF 50/50.
backlog.title: Feature-bagged MLP subspaces

backlog.spec: The QuantileTransformer for the MLP is currently fitted on the training fold only, so the test fold (built from unseen ring skeletons, hence a shifted feature distribution) is mapped through quantiles it does not match. Fit the transform transductively instead: stack Xtr and Xte, call QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(1000, n_rows), random_state=seed).fit on the stacked matrix, then transform the train and test blocks separately for MLP training and prediction. Labels are never touched, so this uses only the test SMILES that the harness already passes in. Keep the RF on the raw feature matrix, keep the 5-seed MLP and the 0.5/0.5 rank average unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive quantile transform fitted on train plus test

backlog.spec: Add a purely instance-based member to the rank blend, which is structurally very different from the forest and the MLP and may add complementary signal on unseen scaffolds. Compute binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test molecules as a dense 0/1 uint8 matrix, then compute the full test-by-train Tanimoto similarity matrix with matrix algebra: inter = Xte @ Xtr.T, sim = inter / (popcount_te[:,None] + popcount_tr[None,:] - inter) with a small epsilon in the denominator. For each test molecule take its k=25 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity cubed, to sharpen). Rank-normalize this prediction and average it with the rank-normalized RF and MLP predictions using weights 0.3 RF, 0.45 MLP, 0.25 kNN. This is cheap (a single 1300x300 matrix product per fold) so runtime should barely change.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-similarity kNN as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Before training each MLP member, create an augmented copy of the quantile-normal training matrix with 2x as many rows. Each new row is a convex combination of two random training rows, with mixing weight lam drawn from Beta(0.4, 0.4) per row (seeded by the seed argument). Its target is the same lam-weighted mix of the two 0/1 labels. Because MLPClassifier needs hard labels, train an MLPRegressor on the soft targets (clipped to [0,1]) with the same hidden sizes and alpha, and use its output clipped to [0,1] as the MLP score. Keep the 5-seed averaging and rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation for MLP training

backlog.spec: Use an inner 3-fold StratifiedKFold on the training data to get out-of-fold RF and MLP predictions (use 2 MLP seeds to save time). Pick the blend weight w in {0.2,0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8} that maximizes inner OOF AUROC of the rank blend. Then fit on the full train fold and blend with w. Keep total runtime under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Rank blend weights tuned by inner CV

backlog.spec: Give the MLP half of the blend more variance reduction by bagging over data as well as over initialization. Replace the loop of 5 MLPClassifiers trained on the full training fold with a loop of 10 MLPClassifiers, where each one is fit on a bootstrap resample of the training rows (draw len(y) indices with replacement using np.random.default_rng(seed + i), and skip/redraw a resample that happens to contain only one class). Keep hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=200, random_state=seed + i. Average the 10 predicted probabilities, then rank-average 0.5/0.5 with the unchanged RF as before.
backlog.title: Bootstrap-bagged MLP ensemble

backlog.spec: Add sklearn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier, which has not been tried yet, as a third equally weighted member of the rank blend alongside the existing RF and 5-seed MLP. Use HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=seed) fitted on the same descriptor+pharmacophore matrix as the RF (it handles the many sparse binary pharmacophore columns natively and is fast on 8 threads). Rank-normalize all three prediction vectors with rankdata/len and average them with weights 1/3 each. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: HistGradientBoosting as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Before fitting any model, compute Tanimoto similarity on Morgan radius-2 bits among the training molecules only. Drop any training molecule that has a training neighbour with similarity at least 0.9 and a different label (conflicting near-duplicates), keeping the others. This removes label noise from close analogue pairs. Train all members on the reduced set, and predict on the full test set. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Near-duplicate training molecule removal

backlog.spec: LightGBM scored 0.0903 as a third blend member but has never replaced the tree half of the two-member blend, where it would carry more weight. Swap RandomForestClassifier out for LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.01, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=5, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, reg_lambda=1.0, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) fit on the same descriptors + Gobbi feature matrix, and take predict_proba[:, 1] as the tree score. Keep the 5-seed MLP and the 0.5/0.5 rank average unchanged. The very low learning rate with heavy column subsampling is the regime that usually suits a few-thousand-feature, 1300-row fold; confirm the 15 fits finish inside 10 minutes and cut n_estimators if not.
backlog.title: Deeper, lower-learning-rate LightGBM replaces the RF

backlog.spec: Keep the current features and MLP exactly as they are, but make the tree side an average of two decorrelated forests instead of one. Fit the existing RandomForestClassifier(300 trees, max_features=0.3, leaf 1, random_state=seed) and additionally an ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=700, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed+1). Rank-normalize each of the three prediction vectors (RF, ET, 5-seed MLP) with rankdata/len and combine with weights 0.25 RF, 0.25 ET, 0.50 MLP, so the tree half is split between the two forest types. This tests whether the one good ExtraTrees result is real while hedging against its observed fragility.
backlog.title: Three-way tree blend: ExtraTrees + RF + MLP

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a 300-tree RandomForest (seed-controlled) on the training fold only, using the full descriptor plus pharmacophore matrix. Keep the top 300 columns by impurity importance and use only those columns for the quantile transform and the 5-seed MLP. The RF in the blend keeps the full feature set. Selection must use training-fold labels only, so no leakage across folds. Keep the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: In-fold importance-based feature selection before the MLP

backlog.spec: Add a feature block that has not been tried: the Avalon fingerprint, which is a substructure-plus-path style descriptor distinct from both Morgan and the Gobbi pharmacophore. In featurize, import from rdkit.Avalon import pyAvalonTools and for each molecule compute pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(mol, nBits=1024), convert it to a dense float vector of length 1024 (loop over the non-zero elements via GetNonzeroElements), apply np.log1p to damp large counts, and hstack it after the existing cleaned descriptor block and Gobbi pharmacophore block. Wrap the per-molecule call in a try/except that returns zeros so a parse failure cannot crash a fold. Leave the RF, MLP and rank blend untouched.
backlog.title: Append Avalon fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: After computing the descriptor+Gobbi matrix on the training fold, drop descriptor columns with zero variance. Then drop one of each pair of descriptor columns with absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95 (computed on the train fold only). Apply the same column mask to the test matrix. Use the filtered matrix for both the RF and the MLP.
backlog.title: Correlation filter on descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit the current RF+MLP blend once. Then take the test molecules whose blended rank-probability is in the top 20% or bottom 20%, and label them 1 or 0. Add them to the training set with those labels. Refit the RF and MLPs on the augmented set and return the final blend predictions for the test molecules.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training

backlog.spec: In the MLP branch, fit the QuantileTransformer on the stacked matrix of training and test features (unlabelled test rows are only used to define the marginal distributions; no labels are used), then transform train and test with that fitted transformer. The RF branch keeps raw features. Keep the 5-seed MLP and the rank blend unchanged. This is a transductive preprocessing step that is legitimate because the harness provides the test SMILES at predict time.
backlog.title: Transductive quantile fitting on train plus test features

backlog.spec: Replace the final rank-averaging with a geometric-mean blend of probabilities. Convert the RF probabilities and the averaged MLP probabilities to logit space (clipped to [1e-4, 1-1e-4]), average the two logits with weights 0.5 each, and map back through the sigmoid. Return the sigmoid output as the score. Keep all members and seeds unchanged. This tests whether keeping calibrated magnitudes helps over pure rank order.
backlog.title: Probability averaging with a geometric mean instead of rank averaging

memo: Helped: only big moves. Morgan+RF (0.1361) to quantile-transformed descriptors with SVC (0.1282/0.1277); adding the Gobbi pharmacophore fingerprint (0.1072); rank-blending RF with a 5-seed MLP (0.0926, incumbent). Nearly everything since was within noise (sd about 0.0049): XGBoost 0.0923, LightGBM 0.0903, CatBoost 0.0907, Tanimoto SVC 0.0909, MACCS 0.0914, log1p Morgan counts 0.0900. Worse: logistic regression 0.1037, FCFP 0.0967, stacking 0.0966, caching 0.0941, MQN/Gasteiger 0.0939, Morgan replacing Gobbi 0.0969, dropping Gobbi 0.0976, varied MLPs 0.0945. ExtraTrees replacing RF gave 0.0890 once, but other variants gave 0.0972, 0.0973 and 0.0947, so it is fragile. Several slots were wasted on aborted repeat ideas and 5 crashed (likely time or memory); check the history before proposing, and keep runtime under 10 minutes. Next: replicate ExtraTrees 0.0890 once; if it holds, combine it with log1p Morgan counts (0.0900). Avoid small swaps and untried feature repeats.
